state.brief: Judge a narrow syntax change for canlang: omitting lowercase then in scenario definitions. The language is generated by AI for CRUD-oriented company SaaS. Its governing goal is adoption, supported by economical tokens, reliable generation and low complexity. A user suggestion motivates evaluation without demonstrating that removal is sound. Executable language tools and empirical token/agent results are absent. Leave scenario declarations, capitalized Given/When/Then, one-space nesting and the rejected general line-minimization proposal outside this change.
state.facts: An operation header specifies typed inputs and either by for callers or on for verified sources. Leading require checks can precede a then introducer. Its inline form accepts semicolon-separated simple statements, and its block form nests locals, checks, state/external effects, results, conditionals and bounded loops. Blocks currently increase depth by one space. Transactional mutation failure discards staged effects and deliveries even if a require follows other work; then does not create atomicity. Pure read operations retain their return/type restrictions. Across sources there are 254 scenarios with 254 lowercase introducers, comprising 154 block markers and 100 inline markers. Thirty-four checks occur within then bodies, so the marker does not separate all checks from all actions. # annotations attach descriptions, while examples tables hold authored expected observations and are excluded from production.
state.candidate: The alternative makes ordered executable statements immediate descendants of the retained scenario signature. Inline marker removal leaves its simple action sequence in place. A block-marker removal outdents the enclosed subtree once while keeping relative branch/loop nesting. Reserve examples as scenario-attached testing syntax and keep its table isolated from execution. The rewrite is required to preserve guards at their actual positions, action order, variable scopes, returned values, caller/source authority and rollback. It must neither pull every require ahead of effects nor merge field writes. Whether a migration meets these requirements must be established rather than stipulated.
state.comparison: Direct-body advantages may be a shorter recurring spelling, fewer container lines/depth and consistent ordering of initial and later checks. Direct-body disadvantages may be erroneous scope flattening, additional syntax/diagnostic adaptation, and confusion between testing children and production children unless the reserved examples rule is enforced. The current wrapper can help identify an action region and provide a dedicated parse container around it and outside examples. Its disadvantages are one mandatory word per operation and, for block uses, 154 lines with another nesting layer; it does not establish a universal guard-first phase. Neither approach has measured tokenizer or generation performance. Each would replace the other as the canonical format, and neither proposal packs arbitrary statements together.

examples.proposed:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 let selected=item.Part
 require count(selected)>0
 for part in selected limit=100
  require part.ready
  set part {done=true}
 set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done
examples.existing:
scenario finish(item:Item) by=members
 require item.status==open
 then
  let selected=item.Part
  require count(selected)>0
  for part in selected limit=100
   require part.ready
   set part {done=true}
  set item {status=done}
 examples item=fixture_item
  item.status -> item.status
  open -> done

state.limits: The paired fragments use illustrative models and a fixture to show the intended scopes, not to claim successful execution. Consider both costs and gains based on these facts. Express the requested property as a NOUL probability without treating it as approval to edit sources.

remove_then.instructions: Do the described direct scenario bodies merit replacing the lowercase then container as canonical syntax after considering both its compactness gains and possible parsing/migration errors?
